question: Should published version changelogs be correctable, and which roles may create an audited correction for skill versions and package releases?
rationale: Published release metadata participates in provenance and trust, so source inspection cannot safely determine whether it should be owner-editable, staff-only, append-only, or immutable.

options.title: Audited owner corrections
options.body: Let the owning user or authorized publisher role add a visible correction while preserving the original text, actor, reason, timestamp, and revision history.

options.title: Staff-only corrections
options.body: Keep release metadata immutable for owners and allow guarded moderator or administrator corrections only for exceptional mistakes.

options.title: Immutable release records
options.body: Require a replacement release or visible addendum rather than changing an existing version record.

recommendation.title: Audited owner corrections
recommendation.body: Let the owning user or authorized publisher role add a visible correction while preserving the original text, actor, reason, timestamp, and revision history.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the versioning, ownership, and audit contract represented in the product specification and registry implementation.
